_doc: SAMPLE lists for the public copy of Avallone. The live shard's lines for off-stage relatives (what became of them) and for homes are hand-written and kept private; these invented lines show the shape. class says whom a line suits (a child, a youth, a grown relative, a dead one), place where that relative may live, work whether the line names a way of earning a living, quarrel whether it is a falling-out.

fates.text: blows glass beads for necklaces
tunes harps for wandering minstrels
binds books in green leather
makes kites and flies the finest one personally
grinds lenses for spectacles
makes horsehair wigs for vain old gentlemen
trains falcons for a baron
engraves names on tankards
sharpens scissors at fairs
draws coastlines for a chart-maker
repairs clocks and is late for everything
looks after a lighthouse and counts the gulls
presses flowers and frames them for sale
paints portraits of prize pigs
is famous for the best plum jam in three parishes
whistles badly and does not care who hears
knows forty riddles and tells them in the wrong order
collects odd-shaped pebbles and labels them
is saving up for a telescope
has a tame magpie and blames it for anything missing
wins every skittles match and is insufferable about it
can name every star visible at midsummer
broke off contact after a dispute over a misplaced ladle
is still sore about a copper kettle promised long ago
was not invited to a wedding and has mentioned it at every meeting since
digs for amber on a far beach
pilots a barge loaded with salt
teaches arithmetic at a temple school far off
feeds a camp of quarrymen up in the mountains
copies manuscripts in a faraway library
sailed off after a row about an inheritance and answers no messages
lives two lanes over and crosses to the far pavement to avoid a hello
collects beetles in a jar and has named each one
has decided to become a dragon and practises roaring
refuses to wear anything but a paper crown
is teaching the cat to dance, without success
sweeps a glassblower's workshop and dreams of the furnace
carries the pole for a lamplighter and yawns all day
was taken by the pox in a bad year
choked on a cherry stone
slipped away in the dark after weeks abed
never woke from a bad turn at midsummer
faded during a wet April, and no physician could say why
was swept off a cliff path by a gale
went through thin ice on a pond
ate the wrong mushrooms
was buried by a rockslide at the quarry
was gored by a bull while droving

homes.text: an attic over a spice-seller's, scented with pepper
a cabin at the end of a muddy lane
a loft reached by an outside staircase
a low dwelling with a green gate and a leaky gutter
half of a divided building, the calmer half
a converted dovecote, round, with nowhere to stand a cupboard
a crowded dwelling where somebody is always awake
a floor split with relatives, with a queue for the wash basin
the family's first dwelling, with initials cut in the lintel
the old birthplace, patched many times
